messages:
anya: quick heads-up — noticed a spike in GH Actions queueing for eval-nightly on ubuntu-latest, several runs timed out and some artifact uploads failed :grimacing:
jordan: ugh, any logs? where is it getting stuck — runner checkout, matrix build, or upload?
gha-bot: Workflow triggered: eval-nightly (branch: main). Status: queued. Runners available: 0 for label 'ubuntu-latest'. Queue position: 12.
anya: minimal logs show long wait before the first job starts, then several jobs run but upload-artifact step hits 504 while contacting uploads.s3.amazonaws.com — suspect network throttling + runner churn
devex: hmm. two quick ideas: 1) add jitter to the cron so all org nightly jobs don't collide, 2) move heavy quantization steps to a dedicated self-hosted label (eval-heavy) and keep smoke checks on GH-hosted
mike: agree with devex. also we can use concurrency group to avoid duplicate runs on same ref: ```yaml
concurrency:
  group: eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
anya: nice, that would help PR gating storms too. but how do we handle nightly vs PR priority? PRs should get precedence for CI quota
sre-bot: org runner capacity is limited during business hours; non-critical nightly jobs should be scheduled with lower priority. Suggest: schedule nightly at randomized minute window and tag with 'low-priority' which our autoscaler deprioritizes. Also monitor runner provisioning failures (rate-limit responses from cloud provider).
jordan: for immediate mitigation, can we split the eval matrix so artifact uploads happen from a single aggregator job? e.g., child jobs write to workspace and aggregator uploads once to reduce parallel S3 requests
devex: yep, pattern: each matrix job writes results to the runner disk, then use a final job with needs: [matrix] that runs on a single runner to collect and upload. Example step: ```yaml
jobs:
  run-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix: {target: [cpu, gpu, quant]}
    steps: [..write outputs to ./artifacts/${{ matrix.target }}]
  upload-agg:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: run-matrix
    steps:
      - name: collect
        run: tar -czf all-results.tgz artifacts/*
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: eval-results
          path: all-results.tgz
```
mike: small note — doing aggregator means we need larger disk on the aggregator runner, watch for runner size limits. also set `actions/upload-artifact` chunk-size to 8MiB to reduce concurrent S3 PUT issues
anya: good call. I'll prototype split-matrix+aggregator as a PR for the nightly workflow. I'll also add a randomized cron window (*/10 for minute range) and a feature flag to flip aggregator on/off.
jordan: can you add a short smoke job at the start that fails fast on infra issues? if that fails, we cancel the rest with the GH API to avoid wasting queue slots
anya: yes — adding a workspace-check step that verifies free disk and s3 reachability. if it fails, we call the cancel API.
sre-bot: we'll also temporarily bump org self-hosted pool for weekend to drain backlog. Monitoring alert: create grafana panel for 'gha queued time' and 'artifact upload errors' so we can measure regressions.
anya: thanks — plan: PR with matrix split + aggregator + concurrency + randomized cron. I'll post link when ready and schedule 30m sync if we need to adjust autoscaler. :thumbsup:
